citations.F1: `serialize_event` does one `SELECT ... FROM users` per event — for 1000 events that's 1000 round trips; batch-fetch actors with a single `WHERE id = ANY($1)`
citations.F3: `lookup_geo` uses synchronous `requests.get` inside an async endpoint, blocking the event loop for up to 2 s per uncached IP
citations.F4: no index on `(org_id, created_at)` — the SELECT does a full scan of 4.2M rows filtered/sorted in memory; add `CREATE INDEX events_org_created_idx ON events (org_id, created_at DESC)`
citations.F5: `_request_timings` is also an unbounded list appended on every request forever — bound or roll it into a proper metrics counter
citations.F6: `_geo_cache` is an unbounded module-level dict keyed by every client IP ever seen, never evicted ... bound it (LRU with a cap/TTL)
citations.F7: After 2–6 are done, re-measure p95 for acme/northwind
citations.F9: don't ship it as-is — more workers/pool connections just let more of the same slow, memory-leaking requests run concurrently ... only then consider a short-TTL response cache (30–60 s) as a smoothing layer, not a substitute
